facts.text: Bloomfield sits in the rolling Shawnee Hills, where fertile silt loam supports corn, wheat, and fruit farms that have fed the region since the 1800s.
The town’s name comes from its central position in Johnson County, a fact noted when Cache Township was renamed Bloomfield in 1819 during a county court session.
Religious roots trace back to 1868 when Pleasant Ridge Presbyterian Church was founded, and 1874 when the Bloomfield Methodist Episcopal Church first met in a schoolhouse.
Early commerce featured a 1875 general store built by Hiram Worley, which originally served as a Grange hall before becoming a local trading hub.
Levi Casey, an Irish immigrant from Tennessee, was one of Bloomfield’s first settlers, arriving in 1808 and establishing a homestead near Casey’s Spring, one of the county’s oldest burial sites.
Bloomfield’s elevation of about 420 feet places it within a temperate climate that historically supported mixed farming and limited horticulture across the county.
